clue.text: Pimp contracted embittered young man

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the word for embittered loses its final letter

parts.note: embittered means sour
a pup is a cheeky or conceited young man

explanation.surface: A pimp is sketched as a shrunken, bitter youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pimp' is the slang verb for customising a car, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to pimp a car is to modify it for show or power, the same as souping it up.

clue.text: Best known expert

parts.note: a secret that is out is known
a gun is an expert, as in a top gun or a gun shearer

explanation.surface: The best-known specialist in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' reads as an adjective with 'known'; it is the verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to best a rival is to defeat them, to have more firepower than them.

clue.text: Pair Maced horrifically might require one

definitions.text: Pair Maced horrifically might require one

indicators.note: horrifically suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Two people sprayed with Mace in a nasty attack might need emergency medical help.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people hurt by a chemical spray would need an ambulance worker trained in emergency care.

clue.text: Schedule for king once — in the morning meeting compiler

indicators.note: meeting says the last piece joins on directly after the one before

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
GR, Georgius Rex, is a former king's royal cipher
AM, ante meridiem, is the morning
the setter, or compiler, refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A timetable for an old king, with a morning appointment with the crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a programme of events is a schedule or plan of what happens when.

clue.text: Splendid friend, regularly a stoic ally

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words a stoic ally, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine companion who is a steadfast, uncomplaining ally.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: palatial means grand or magnificent like a palace, hence splendid.

clue.text: Sound made by tiny feet on northern model

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: the patter of tiny feet is the noise of small children running about

explanation.surface: The pitter-patter of little feet on a northern catwalk model.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pattern is a model or template to be copied.

clue.text: Kindle is not difficult to carry

definitions.meaning: to kindle is to set a fire going, to ignite it
something easy to carry weighs little

explanation.surface: A Kindle e-reader is easy to carry around.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to ignite a fire, and of little weight.

clue.text: More loyal lorry-driver, not fickle at heart

indicators.note: not says the letters that follow are taken away from the driver

parts.note: a trucker drives a lorry

indicators.note: at heart means the two central letters of the word fickle

explanation.surface: A steadfast truck driver who never wavers in his affections.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative synonym: truer means more faithful or steadfast.

clue.text: Unit for measuring liquid — not grams

indicators.note: liquid means fluid, not fixed, so the letters of not grams flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A measure for liquids that is not given in grams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit for measuring liquid' looks like the definition; 'liquid' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a tiny unit of length, a ten-billionth of a metre, used for wavelengths and atomic sizes.

clue.text: Tutor sat prepared to begin

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of tutor sat are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher sits ready to begin the lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb synonym: to start out is to set off or begin.

clue.text: Envy good and simple Dickensian

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge, the title character of a Dickens novel, is a simple-minded young man

explanation.surface: Jealousy of a decent, unsophisticated Dickens character.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to grudge someone something is to resent or begrudge their having it.

clue.text: Recalled difficulty receiving Madame's bad reaction

indicators.note: receiving means the reversed word takes the next piece inside it
recalled means called back, so the word for difficulty is read backwards

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in there's the rub
Mme is the abbreviation for Madame

explanation.surface: Remembering a problem that drew a sharp response from a French lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: a bummer is a disappointing thing, the response to bad news, as in what a downer.

clue.text: Sum being divided by figure minus two-thirds

indicators.note: divided by means the word for being is split apart by the next piece

parts.note: an entity is a being

indicators.note: minus two-thirds means the word figure loses the first four of its six letters

explanation.surface: An arithmetic sum: some quantity divided by a number, less two-thirds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a number to find; the word itself is trimmed to its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the entirety is the whole amount, the sum of everything.

clue.text: Wicked person's backstabber — I must leave shower

parts.note: a demon is a wicked person; the 's adds S

indicators.note: must leave says the letter I is taken out of the word for backstabber

parts.note: a traitor stabs friends in the back

explanation.surface: A villainous betrayer insists the speaker get out of the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is one who shows, not a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who shows how a product or procedure works is literally a shower of it.

clue.text: Singer eating a steak in regular chunks is not fatal

indicators.note: eating means the singer takes the next piece inside

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano singer

indicators.note: in regular chunks means every other letter of the words a steak

explanation.surface: A singer choking on a steak cut into even pieces survives.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or wound that can be cured is not fatal; the answer's 'is' is absorbed by the predicate adjective.

clue.text: Cut the bacon I cooked

indicators.note: cooked means fiddled or altered, so the letters of the bacon I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A butcher points to the bacon he has just cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the aitchbone is a butcher's cut of beef from the rump, around the hip bone.

clue.text: Show much appreciation verbally for women's garment

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so what is said is matched by sound

parts.note: to coo lots is to show plenty of delight or admiration

explanation.surface: Praising a woman's outfit out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: culottes are women's knee-length trousers cut full to look like a skirt.

clue.text: Processed food from can, hotel menu misrepresented

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown falsely, so the letters are shown in a different order

explanation.surface: A hotel menu passes off tinned food as something finer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is processed, cooked pork in a block, usually tinned and sliced cold.

clue.text: Training set up European with routine work

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the pieces are written bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine
to run a machine is to work it

explanation.surface: A European trainee set up with drills and routine work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: nurture is the upbringing, training or education that shapes someone.

clue.text: Vote during year in France for extension

indicators.note: during means the vote falls within the French year

parts.note: année is French for year
X is the mark put on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A French vote held that year on building an extension.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an annexe is a building added on, an extension.

clue.text: Judge alcoholic drink containing fruity nose, mostly

indicators.note: containing means the drink holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: fruity suggests something juicy and mixed up, so the letters are jumbled
mostly means the word nose loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A wine judge assesses a drink with a fruity nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' and 'fruity nose' suggest a wine show; the judge is the verb meaning to deem.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to consider is to think over, to judge or deem.

clue.text: Cats reviewed, based on Eliot's capital poetic hit

indicators.note: based on in a down clue means the first piece rests on top of the next
reviewed means looked at again backwards, so the word for cats is reversed

parts.note: toms are male cats

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of Eliot's

explanation.surface: A review of the musical Cats, based on T S Eliot's poems, calls it a poetic hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic or literary past tense of smite, so a struck blow in poetry.

clue.text: Little is taken in by dumb vacant nerd

indicators.note: is taken in by means this piece goes inside the letters that follow
vacant means emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters of dumb

parts.note: wee means little

explanation.surface: A small dim-witted nerd is easily fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a dweeb is a socially awkward, boring person, a geek.

clue.text: Middle-eastern ingredient not abundant around area west of Italy

indicators.note: west of in an across clue means the first piece comes to the left
around means the scanty word wraps round the next letter

parts.note: thin means scanty, not abundant
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern ingredient in short supply in a region west of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a sesame-seed paste used throughout Middle Eastern cooking, as in hummus.

clue.text: Futile notions to sacrifice two knights before end of game

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the next
to sacrifice means giving pieces up, so letters leave the word notions

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight, so two give NN

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of game

explanation.surface: A chess player's notion of giving up both knights before the endgame is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: otiose means serving no purpose, pointless or futile.

clue.text: French article suitable to put in gun is not surpassed

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article

indicators.note: to put in means this piece goes inside the gun

parts.note: a Bren is a British light machine gun
OK means acceptable, suitable

explanation.surface: A French item fit to be loaded into a gun is unrivalled.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbroken record is one that nobody has beaten or surpassed.

clue.text: Spring lamb sees flock

indicators.note: spring means leap about, so the letters of lamb sees jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A spring lamb looks at a flock of sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring lamb' reads as a season's lamb; 'Spring' is the anagram signal, and 'flock' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to flock is to gather together in a crowd, to assemble.

clue.text: Made regular eleven edgier to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A football eleven grows more nervous and is brought back into line.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to even out a surface or score is to make it level or uniform.
